block:
--- Authentication.md ---
Accounts
How you authenticate depends on how the server is running:

* **Multi-space mode (the default).** A fresh install manages accounts and controls who can reach each space. This is the recommended setup — see [[#Accounts]].
* **Single-space mode.** One folder served as one space, authenticated by a single set of environment-variable credentials — see [[#Single-space mode]].
* **No authentication.** A single-space server with no credentials set is open to anyone who can reach it.

--- Account.md ---
Account
Each account has a username, a login method (local password or SSO), an admin flag, any number of API tokens, and a profile (an optional full name and email used for attribution), which the account holder can edit themselves, or an admin can set on their behalf.

* **Admins** can reach the admin UI and manage spaces, accounts, and tokens. They can also log into *every* space.
* **Non-admin accounts** are ordinary users: they can log into any space they are a member of, and any space whose access level admits them (see [[Dashboard#Access]]).

There is no self-service signup. Admins create accounts. There is no password recovery either, an admin sets a new password from the _Users_ tab. Administrators can also provision [[Single Sign-On|SSO accounts]] alongside local accounts.

--- HTTP API.md ---
Authentication | Profile
* `GET /.accounts`: Every account with access to this space, as `[{"username", "fullName", "me"}]`, with the caller’s own entry marked `me`. `username` is `null` where the deployment keeps no accounts (the caller is still reported, marked `me`, so their name is known even though they are nobody the space can address), `fullName` is omitted when unset, and `me` is omitted when false.

--- Install/Server Modes.md ---
Single-space mode | Single-space mode
Single-space mode serves one folder with one optional login configured through `SB_USER`.

* It has no multiple-account management or per-member space roles.
* [[Revisions]] has limited configuration, including remote Git setup.
* [[Single Sign-On]] is unavailable.
* Mentions still support ad-hoc and API-defined identities. Account-based completion is unavailable.

Use [[Install/Configuration]] for legacy environment variables. Without authentication, anyone who can reach the server can access the space. Migrate to multi-space mode for account-managed sharing.

--- Install/Configuration.md ---
Network | Legacy “single-space” mode options > Authentication
* `SB_USER` (single-space only): Sets single-user credentials, in `username:password` form. Use a long password and protect the process configuration.
* `SB_AUTH_TOKEN` (single-space only): Enables `Authorization: Bearer <token>` style authentication on the [[HTTP API]]. In multi-space mode this is replaced by per-account [[Authentication#API|API tokens]].
* `SB_LOCKOUT_LIMIT`: Specifies the number of failed login attempt before locking the user out (for a `SB_LOCKOUT_TIME` specified amount of seconds), defaults to `10`
* `SB_LOCKOUT_TIME`: Specifies the amount of time (in seconds) a client will be blocked until attempting to log back in, defaults to `60`.
* `SB_REMEMBER_ME_HOURS`: Sets the session duration in hours when “Remember me” is checked during login, defaults to 7 days. Sessions where “Remember me” was left unchecked always last one week.
